title: EU Sovereign Tech Fund Survey
content:
Take the survey now

The survey is a short questionnaire that takes about 15 minutes to complete. It is designed to gather evidence on critical open source components, and the sustainability issues that they face. It also aims to better understand the views and priorities of people in open-source communities and projects. The resulting data will be used to shape the EU Sovereign Tech Fund pilot.

title: The Digital Commons EDIC adopts joint strategy to scale open-source alternatives
content:
The Assembly of Members adopts a 2026–2027 strategy to make open-source tools easier to deploy and sustain, approves Poland’s accession as a Member State, welcomes Croatia and Norway as Observers and appoints an Advisory Board.

At its meeting on 16 October 2026, the Assembly of Members of the Digital Commons EDIC adopted its Implementation Strategy for 2026–2027.

Organisations across Europe often tackle similar integration, procurement and maintenance challenges separately. The strategy brings countries, businesses and open-source communities together to share expertise, reduce duplicated effort and make successful deployments easier to repeat.

title: The Digital Commons EDIC moves into Campus Cyber, bringing European digital commons closer to cybersecurity expertise
content:
PRESS RELEASE

Puteaux, 9 October 2026 — The Digital Commons EDIC inaugurates its offices at Campus Cyber. The consortium, hosted by France, brings together five European countries — France, Germany, the Netherlands, Italy and Luxembourg — and seven observers, to support the development and maintenance of open-source digital tools. Its arrival brings this European cooperation closer to businesses, public-sector organisations and researchers specialising in cybersecurity, whose expertise will help to make sure that open-source software components are dependable and secure in practice.

title: Digital Commons EDIC launches first operational activities at Paris kick-off
content:
Paris, 19 June 2026 – The Digital Commons EDIC (European Digital Infrastructure Consortium) today held the official kick-off of its first implementation activities, bringing together representatives from Member States, the European Commission, open source communities, and industry partners in Paris.

The event marks the Digital Commons EDIC’s transition from setup to operational delivery, following the European Commission’s recent Tech Sovereignty package and EU Open Source Strategy, which identify open source and digital commons as central to Europe’s technological sovereignty and name the Digital Commons EDIC as a practical cooperation vehicle for Member States.

title: Digital Commons EDIC welcomes Europe's new tech sovereignty agenda
content:
The Digital Commons EDIC warmly welcomes the European Commission’s new European Technological Sovereignty Package and EU Open Source Strategy.

The package confirms that open source and digital commons are now part of Europe’s strategic infrastructure agenda. They are essential to Europe’s capacity to act, choose, innovate, and remain resilient in critical digital domains.

“The Commission’s Open Source Strategy positions the Digital Commons EDIC as a practical cooperation vehicle for Member States to develop, adopt, and scale secure open source alternatives across Europe,” says Art de Blaauw, CIO Central Government of The Netherlands and Chair of the Assembly of Members. “That gives our work a very concrete direction: move from policy momentum to concrete implementation, with shared projects, sustainable maintenance, and real users.”

title: Digital Commons EDIC takes shape with more countries, director and first projects
content:
The Digital Commons European Digital Infrastructure Consortium (EDIC) is taking shape with more countries joining, a newly appointed Director and its first projects, including a pilot for a European Sovereign Tech Fund. The DC-EDIC supports EU Member States in developing open digital infrastructure and strengthening Europe’s digital sovereignty.

The DC-EDIC is part of the Digital Decade programme. It supports cooperation between EU Member States in developing joint digital projects, with the aim of strengthening Europe’s digital sovereignty. The DC-EDIC focuses on digital commons, open-source software, and shared digital infrastructure. It serves as a single point of contact for developers, public organisations, and open-source communities, helping them access funding and initiate new projects. One example is the development of a European digital workspace.
